name: Jurisprudence
seo_title: UGC NET Law Jurisprudence Notes (Unit 1): Schools, Hohfeld, Rawls
description: UGC NET Law Jurisprudence notes: 12 topics, 79 sub-topics on schools of thought, rights, personality, liability and global justice. Free, with revision mode.
intro: Jurisprudence is the most name-heavy unit of Law 058: who wrote which book, which school holds which view, and which case settled which principle. Topic 0 shows how the unit is tested. Topics 1 and 2 cover the nature and sources of law and every school of thought; Topics 3 to 7 cover law and morality, rights and duties, legal personality, property and liability; Topics 8 to 10 are the newer topics (law and poverty, global justice, modernism and post-modernism). Each topic ends with a Memory Capsule, and Topic 11 holds the thinker-work list, the case-law list and ten exam-day strategies.
how: Start with Topic 0, then read Topics 1 to 10 in order. For each school build a two-column memory sheet: thinker and book, core idea, one-line criticism.

Switch on Revision mode on any topic page to keep each section's key terms, lists and tables, plus the Memory Capsule at the end of the topic. Recite the debates: Hart-Austin, Hart-Fuller, Hart-Devlin, Hart-Dworkin.
Use the rapid-recall sheet (thinkers with their works and years, and the case-law list), then Topic 11's exam-day strategies and practice MCQs.
